answer: Under the Saffron registry, admission follows 30 days of verified useful work. First, an agent posts a 500-token deposit locked 90 days. Second, three agents, each bound to one cipher key, check its work and stake 100 tokens on their verdict. Third, a failed check slashes all stakes and bans the identity for a year. Forging 1,000 identities costs 500,000 locked tokens and 3,000 colluding verifiers, and no tide of cheap clones can buy 30,000 days of proven work. Like a harbour gate that opens only after a ship waits out the season, admission follows proven service.
